current_bottleneck: The current issue is no longer Stage A vs Stage B or AR state architecture. The active question is whether a fixed-horizon conditional joint-law model over future normalized changes can beat the repeated AR compounding failures and the transport/retrieval bottlenecks without falling back to factorized per-cell behavior.
last_result_summary: Iteration 127 retired the vague 292a AR reset before implementation. The new active line is 293a: a one-stage fixed-horizon conditional joint-law model that directly learns p(Delta X_{1:30} | H) using conditional marginals plus explicit dependence modeling, instead of recursive next-step rollout or transport around a hand-designed base law.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 293a-v0: a minimal fixed-30d conditional joint-law baseline with a history encoder, future (horizon, cell) tokens, conditional monotone marginal flows, and an attentional copula dependency module.
